findings.problem: In the frame "call me [any] day" the word comes before a noun, so the right Spanish is cualquier (llámame cualquier día), not the answer shown, cualquiera, and a learner who recalls cualquier would be marked wrong, or would learn that cualquiera día is correct.
findings.fix: en: pick [any one] of them; hint: any one at all, whichever, not a person (that is the anyone card)

findings.problem: The sentence is natural and correctly translated, but it uses only the shortened form cualquier, so it does not show es as written and would no longer match a corrected prompt that uses the full form.
findings.fix: example.es: Puedes elegir cualquiera de los dos. example.en: You can pick either one.

back.es: any, any at all, whichever (determiner; cualquier before a noun)

note: Another option is to keep the noun frame and put the word after the noun (un día cualquiera), but that means an ordinary day rather than any day, so the any-one-of-them frame fits better; the hint's note that it shortens to cualquier before a noun is worth keeping on the answer side.
